correctness.rationale: The non-decaying sector of H=JA-iκ|o><o|/2 is exactly the span of hub-orthogonal A-eigenvectors, by a reducing-subspace and negative-imaginary-spectrum argument. At a reduced path frequency b/q, c_q arms support normalized sine modes and the one nonzero hub constraint gives dark dimension c_q−1. Their squared boundary amplitudes scale as 1/L_i; explicit projector diagonals and sum of sine squares yield the Ramanujan expression. Every term is nonnegative, and its vanishing condition is q|t, proving the lcm/gcd criterion and the bright-site count. Direct adjacency-eigenspace numerical checks passed on 715 graphs and 7973 sites (maximum error 2.22e-15); four independent dissipative semigroup samples gave agreement within 1.17e-12 at time 12000. Finite tests supplement, not replace, the all-integer proof.

value.rationale: The central-site detection question is natural in exciton transport along branched pathways. The exact arithmetic result solves which individual initial sites are perfectly capturable despite nontrivial global dark space, provides every site survival probability, and identifies pairwise coprimality of shifted arm lengths as a complete network-design criterion. These are structural, experimentally interpretable invariants and not ad hoc finite tabulations; no downstream theorem of broader scope is claimed.
